title: Book One · Chapter 57: Mr Han's Writing
story:
On Friday afternoon, Mum finds Mr Han at the shoe repair place. Ronan is with her. Leo went home with his mother. He is not there for this talk.

Mum asks to speak a little away from the counter. She shows Mr Han the copy of the brown envelope's outside.

Mr Han checks each part. He reads the name and the large six. He finds his small Han at the bottom.

“That's my writing,” he says.

Ronan looks up at Mr Han. Mr Han knows his own writing. The sender is Mr Han. That is certain now.

Mr Han explains the money. A relative of his stayed nearby. Mrs Gao paid for some meals. Mr Han is paying her back. He put a small amount in the envelope. He also put an address paper inside. Mrs Gao can keep that paper.

“A neighbour offered to take it. His route went past East Court,” he says. “I did not check the entrance with him. That was my mistake.”

“Did he take it to the wrong green gate?” Ronan asks.

“It appears so. I did not ask him about that yet.”

Mr Han doesn't call the neighbour careless or dishonest. “Some of my letters run together,” he says. “That can confuse people, too.” He writes slowly on a new piece of paper: MRS GAO, 6 EAST COURT. He writes a note for Mrs Lan, too. He writes his name on the note. Then he writes: I SENT THE BROWN ENVELOPE.

Mum asks, “Do you want the envelope back now?”

“Please leave it closed with Mrs Lan for now. First we need to find Mrs Gao's door. We may not find it before Sunday. Then I will collect it myself. The children should not carry this money.”

Mum repeats the plan to check it. Mrs Lan will keep the envelope closed. Mum will look for Mrs Gao's door. The right door comes first. Then Mum will check with Mr Han. He can agree to the delivery. No door means no delivery. Then he will collect it on Sunday. He will send it himself.

Ronan likes the new plan. Each adult has a part in the plan. Ronan can help with the map. Mum will look for the right gate with him.

“Did you like Bo's top at your birthday?” Mr Han asks. Ronan tells him about the cat and the chalk circle. Mr Han laughs loudly. The shoe repairer looks over at the sound.

“The cat does not need money for food,” he says. “It eats at three doors.”

On the way home, Ronan asks Mum a question. “Why didn't Mr Han take it himself?”

“He had another job to do,” Mum says. “Sometimes a neighbour carries a letter for us. But he needs the full address. Mr Han and his neighbour did not check it well enough.”

“Would you let me carry it?”

“No. You're helping us make the route clear. The money stays with adults.”

At the yard, Mrs Lan reads Mr Han's note. Then she opens her drawer. She checks the envelope inside. The flap is still closed. Then she puts both papers away together and locks it again.

Later, Leo comes to the gate. Ronan repeats Mr Han's news. “How much money is inside?” Leo asks.

“I don't know. We don't need to count it.”

“Enough for a bike?”

“It isn't bike money.”

Leo looks down. “I know. I was just asking.”

They take out the map. Ronan copies the correct street name carefully. He adds no money sign and no story about the neighbour. The map only needs to help someone reach a door.

Mr Han sent the envelope. They know that now. They also know Mrs Gao's name and address. Mrs Lan is keeping the envelope safe. Tomorrow they can ask about the route. Which way leads to the right door?
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：relative＝亲属；envelope＝信封；sender＝寄出者；collect＝领取。

辅助理解：paying her back＝把她先垫的钱还给她；封内金额尚未由儿童点数。

理解问题：

1. Mr Han 怎样确认信封属于他寄出的那封？
2. 信封中的钱是什么钱，应该由谁处理？
